def factor_tail_fragility_skew_volume(df):
    """Tail fragility captured by negative return skewness amplified by volume concentration on down days."""
    df_copy = df.copy()
    ret = df_copy["close"].pct_change()
    skew = ret.rolling(60, min_periods=30).skew()
    vol_neg = (df_copy["volume"] * (ret < 0)).rolling(60, min_periods=30).sum()
    vol_total = df_copy["volume"].rolling(60, min_periods=30).sum()
    vol_share = vol_neg / vol_total.replace(0.0, np.nan)
    factor = -skew * vol_share
    factor_smooth = factor.ewm(span=10, min_periods=5).mean()
    df_copy["factor_tail_fragility_skew_volume"] = factor_smooth
    return df_copy["factor_tail_fragility_skew_volume"]
description: Captures tail fragility as the product of negative return skewness (left-tail thickness) and volume concentration on negative return days. Rolling 60-day skewness of daily returns is negated so that more negative (left-skewed) distributions produce higher fragility, and then multiplied by the share of volume that occurs on down days. An exponential smoothing span of 10 days preserves stress persistence. This mechanism explores a distinct skew-volume pathway rather than downside magnitude or volatility alone.
